r3.problem: The stable functional API, broad compatibility facade, contracts, validation, versioning, and exception layers overlap more than necessary.

A.title: Staged compatibility-facade retirement
design: Keep pssolver.functional.api and Functional API 1.1 source-compatible throughout v0.4.
Consolidate duplicate internal contracts and helpers behind the stable api facade without changing its exported names or behavior.
Mark direct imports from the broader pssolver.functional compatibility facade as deprecated during v0.4, but keep them operational for the full v0.4 line.

Do not emit a deprecation warning while importing pssolver.functional.api: importing that child loads the current eager pssolver.functional parent. Emit a warning only when a compatibility-facade name is accessed, for example through a module-level __getattr__.
Do not remove the broad facade before a later release with an explicit API-version decision and a separately qualified Consumer migration.
A.deprecation_window: all v0.4 releases; removal no earlier than a later explicitly authorized release

B.title: Internal consolidation without facade retirement
design: Consolidate internals while retaining both pssolver.functional.api and the broad pssolver.functional facade indefinitely.
Avoids deprecation work but leaves the overlapping public surface in place.

C.title: Immediate facade removal and API-version change
design: Remove the broad compatibility facade during v0.4 and change the Functional API version.
Requires an immediate Consumer migration and is not compatible with the frozen S-17 numerical and public-boundary constraints.

control_coordination.coordination_rule: Any later change to pssolver.functional.api names, semantics, or API version, or to either planar constitutive blob, requires an isolated PSSolver-Control main migration and CPU qualification before the provider change can be released.
control_coordination.deprecation_warning_rule: Importing pssolver.functional.api must remain warning-free because Python first imports the eager pssolver.functional parent package. A compatibility-facade deprecation may warn only when the caller accesses a facade name, for example through module-level __getattr__.

research_branch.policy: Keep the research branch and its v0.2.0 provider unchanged; migrate it only in a separate, explicitly scoped qualification.

r6.problem: Robin and finite-Q pilot surfaces span configuration, planning, operators, runtime, and workflows without a publicly qualified application; lifting is adjacent and still has deferred correctness issues.

A.title: Reassess Robin, finite-Q, and lifting together
design: Treat Robin, finite-Q, and lifting as one boundary-pilot family for inventory, ownership, and deprecation decisions.
Keep public execution fail-closed while the audit is performed.
Quarantine unqualified entry points behind an explicitly experimental namespace or remove only unreachable duplicates after a deprecation window.
Do not reopen lifting until B8/S2-07 wall physics and runtime dtype coercion are resolved and independently qualified.
Preserve read-only compatibility for every released checkpoint format even if a pilot writer or entry point is retired.

B.title: Isolate Robin and finite-Q only
design: Audit and isolate Robin and finite-Q now while leaving lifting entirely deferred.
Reduces immediate scope but leaves shared boundary/planning ownership to a later, overlapping migration.

C.title: Immediately remove all pilot and lifting surfaces
design: Delete unqualified Robin, finite-Q, and lifting surfaces in v0.4.
This has the highest compatibility risk and is not allowed without a separate deprecation and checkpoint-compatibility plan.

recommended_implementation_order_after_c: Inventory every public import, internal owner, production caller, fixture, and released checkpoint reader for Robin, finite-Q, and lifting.
Classify each surface as qualified public, required compatibility reader, experimental, duplicate, or unreachable.
Publish deprecations without changing numerical execution or enabling lifting.
Resolve and qualify B8/S2-07 before any lifting execution is reopened.
Only then isolate or remove approved surfaces, with CPU equivalence and checkpoint compatibility gates.
r6.control_impact: The qualified Control adapters import only pssolver.functional.api and do not import Robin, finite-Q, or lifting pilot modules; R6 should not require a Control migration unless it changes that stable functional boundary.

questions_for_user.question: Which R3 facade strategy should govern implementation?
Should any future Functional API change or change to either planar constitutive blob require Control main migration first, while research/3d-warmup remains a separately authorized v0.2.0 migration?

options.A: Yes; preserve the current Functional API and blob-pinned Consumer boundary.
options.B: Allow provider API or planar constitutive blob changes before Control migration.

questions_for_user.question: Should R6 reassess lifting together with Robin and finite-Q?
If the combined audit confirms unqualified entry points, which default disposition should apply?

options.A: Quarantine behind an experimental namespace with deprecation before removal.
options.B: Retain the current public locations indefinitely.
